title: Punt FT%: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt FT% build in our 12-team H2H 9-cat league, and how should they be tiered by auction value? Each line must also note the guard stats (AST, 3PTM, ST, PTS) a player brings, because the experts warn that drafting only bad free throw shooters punts four categories.
summary: Punt FT% works in our league only if you keep buying assists, threes and steals after the big men. Giannis is the anchor at about 60 to 62 USD. Barnes, Sengun, Daniels and Mobley are the core, and the cheap centers (Kessler, Gobert, Claxton) fill rebounds, blocks and FG%. None of the listed targets brings threes, so you must buy 3PTM from guards outside this list, or the build quietly punts four categories.

paragraphs.text: The experts agree on the main risk. Free throws are linked to points, threes and assists. If you draft only bad free throw shooters, you effectively punt four categories, not one. In a 12-team H2H league, losing FT%, 3PTM, AST and PTS most weeks loses the matchup.

The rule for our auction: after you buy a guard-stat-poor anchor like Giannis, two of your next three buys should be players who bring assists, threes or steals. The original advice is 'guards in two of the next three rounds'. In an auction, that means checking your roster after every purchase in the first hour. If you are missing assists or threes, raise your bids on guards, not on another big man.

Check this list before the draft. No player below is credited with threes in the notes. Daniels, Ausar Thompson, Zion, Gobert and Claxton actively hurt 3PTM. So every three you need has to come from players outside this target list. Plan to buy 3PTM with real money in the early and middle rounds.

sections.heading: Do you have to punt FT% with Giannis?

paragraphs.text: The experts disagree here. One side says taking Giannis in round one does not force you to punt free throws or to target other bad shooters. Your targets after him are still every player. The other side says that if you draft a bad free throw shooter like Giannis, you should punt FT% and get guard stats early. His profile note also says to build around punting FT% and accept the turnovers.

Both sides agree on what to do in practice. Do not chase low free throw players for their own sake. Buy the best player at a fair price, and treat poor FT% as a discount you can absorb, not a reason to bid.

Do not push up players who gain value in punt rankings just to secure them. Other managers in our league will also see that Sengun or Kessler rank higher with FT% removed. Set a ceiling before the draft and walk away when it is passed. For example, the notes say not to go above about 30 USD for Sengun, about 12 to 15 USD for Kessler and about 10 USD for Zion.

Overall 9-cat ranks can mislead you. If you punt FT%, a drop in a player's free throw shooting barely matters to you, even if his overall rank falls a lot. That is why Siakam (about 72% FT) and Mobley look better to a punter than to a balanced team. Mobley is worth less in a build that keeps FT%.

Do not choose the punt because of one bad season. FT% swings a lot in both directions, and it is the most variable fantasy category. Price a poor shooter as if his free throws will stay bad, and treat any improvement as a bonus. Mobley is the test case: experts are watching whether his FT% climbs back toward 70%.

The cheap centers in this pool all give the same package: FG%, rebounds and blocks. Buy one or two late instead of paying middle-round prices. Gobert, Kessler and Claxton cover this. Robinson and Nurkic are better left on waivers in our 144-player draft.

A poor free throw shooter who starts is partly protected from hack-a-player fouling, because there are no team fouls early in the game. So in the first weeks, check starting jobs: Claxton ahead of Jalen Smith and Zach Collins, Robinson versus Queta, and Nurkic versus Jaxson Hayes after his return. Use your FAB and the six weekly adds on the one who wins the job.

Check playoff schedules for weeks 19 to 21 before the trade deadline on 2027-03-04. Miami (Giannis) and Houston (Sengun) have weak 10-game playoff schedules, though Miami has no back-to-backs in those weeks. Mobley faces a 2-game finals week. Gobert has a two-game semifinal week. If you hold several of them, plan a deadline trade or streaming adds to cover those weeks.

He is the best second piece next to Giannis because his assists and steals, plus blocks, are rare for an F/C. Check that his assists and shot volume hold next to Kawhi Leonard.
Removing FT% leaves strong points, rebounds and center-spot assists, but he adds no threes or steals per the notes, and his turnovers hurt.
He is a steals outlier with real assists, rebounds and FG%, so he covers two guard stats. His threes are weak, which makes 3PTM a hole you must fill elsewhere.

FT% is his only real hole, so in this build he is a clean blocks, rebounds and FG% asset. He brings little in assists, steals or points by the notes, and his threes depend on 3P% recovering toward 33%.
He is a pure three-category center (blocks, rebounds, FG%). Experts call his recent gains in threes, steals and assists noise, so count on no guard stats from him.
Punt FT and punt TO builds give up little on his weak spots and keep his points, rebounds and forward assists. The notes do not credit him with threes or steals.
He is a steals anchor with good blocks and FG%, but his threes are near zero. His assist upside depends on 28 or more minutes.
He is a solid punt FT piece with F and C eligibility. His assists and usage, his guard-stat contribution, should drop with Haliburton back, so pay only his lower value.
